claims.text: The initial material is a multiphase Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy system.
Phase-field modeling can be used to control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Ab initio or density-functional-theory calculations can be coupled with phase-field modeling for this purpose.
Phase-field modeling can simulate the effects of alloy composition on phase transformations.
Phase-field modeling can simulate the effects of temperature and cooling rate on phase transformations.
Simulating composition and processing effects permits prediction and control of phase evolution.
Optimizing alloy composition and processing conditions through the model will reduce the phase-transformation temperature.
A 10% variation in alloy composition will produce a 20% reduction in phase-transformation temperature relative to uncontrolled phase evolution.
The relevant composition space has each of Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni in the range of 10–30 at.%.
The proposed processing window is 500–1000 °C with cooling rates of 1–10 °C/min.
Model accuracy and the availability of reliable experimental validation data are sources of uncertainty.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted phase-transformation temperature differs from experiment by more than 15%.
The hypothesis is falsified if a 10% composition variation reduces phase-transformation temperature by less than 15%.
